title: Morphologically Chiral 2D Perovskites
excerpt: Achiral layered perovskites grow into twisted and helical ribbons, like opening seed pods.
body:
Our paper on morphologically chiral nanoribbons is published in Nature Synthesis. We show that layered metal-halide perovskites built entirely from achiral molecules spontaneously grow into twisted and helical ribbons. Hydrogen-bonded organic networks within the lattice generate mismatched strains, and the ribbons bend and twist to release them — geometric frustration, the same mechanism that opens chiral seed pods. Controlling growth kinetics twists nearly all ribbons in one direction, giving bulk samples chiroptical activity.

The work was highlighted by the UGA New Materials Institute.

Read More: Morphologically Chiral 2D Materials and Miniaturized Photonics

title: New VIPR Team: Photonic Materials
excerpt: Undergraduates: join our new VIPR team, Photonic Materials from Nanocrystals to Bulk. Apply by Oct 31.
body:
Fall 26 marks the launch of a new UGA Vertically Integrated Projects for Research (VIPR) team, Photonic Materials from Nanocrystals to Bulk, with Prof. Vladislav Klepov and Prof. Tina Salguero. Students on the team design, synthesize, and characterize crystals, and combine spectroscopy, microscopy, and AI-driven data analysis to understand how crystal structure shapes material properties across length scales.

The team is accepting undergraduate applications for Spring 2027 through October 31, 2026. Apply here.

title: Interfacial Steric Hindrance in 2D Perovskites
excerpt: Our invited paper is published in MRS Communications.
body: Our invited research letter, written by Wai Loon, has been published in MRS Communications as part of the Early Career Materials Researchers Special Issue. We investigate hydrogen-bonded organic framework alignment in layered perovskites and show its tunability via both inorganic metal-halide and organic halide substitution, which modulates interfacial steric hindrance. Congratulations to Wai Loon!

title: Air-stable Layered Perovskite Nanolasers
excerpt: Front cover: air stable microlasers was achieve with an "air-unstable" layered perovskite.
body:
Our work with Dr. Sangyeon (Fred) Cho on layered perovskite microlasers was featured on the front cover of ACS Photonics. We report stable room-temperature lasing from quasi-2D tin iodide perovskite microcrystals in ambient air. The cover illustrates plasmonic microlasing from microscale crystals on the gold substrate.

title: Layered Perovskite Room-Temperature Nanolasers
body:
Practical room-temperature (RT) operation of nanowire lasers requires efficient gain materials. Our recent JACS, provided an answer through meticulous crystallization control of phase-pure quasi-2D tin-iodide perovskite nanowires. These nanowires support color-tunable NIR, RT optically pumped lasing, with thresholds as low as 75.8 μJ/cm², cavity quality factors exceeding 3000, and negligible degradation over more than one million pulses. This work opens the door to using layered perovskite nanowires as a promising platform for nanoscale electronics and miniaturized photonic devices. Thanks to all the collaborators!

Read More: Miniaturized Layered Perovskite Lasers.

title: Ionic Liquid x Perovskite Solar Cell
excerpt: New report in Nature Energy with solar cells retain 90% performance at 90°C.
body:
Led by Dr. Wenzhan Xu, our paper using ionic liquids to enhance the stability of perovskite solar cells has been published in Nature Energy. A new ionic liquid MEM-MIM-Cl was used to regulate perovskite growth and stabilize buried interfaces. Solar cells incorporating MEM-MIM-Cl achieved a power conversion efficiency of 25.9% and retained 90% initial performance after 1,500 hrs' 1-sun illumination and 90°C thermal stress - surpassing prior benchmarks under milder ageing conditions. Many thanks to all the collaborators!

Read More: Templated Crystallization in Perovskite Optoelectronics.
